reasons: quran:2:30-39 covers the khilafa announcement, teaching of the names, the angels' prostration, Iblis's refusal, the tree, the descent and Adam's repentance; all about Adam.
Range starts at the natural opening (2:30) and ends before quran:2:40 turns to Bani Israel; nothing relevant cut off.
quran:7:11-25 is the full episode: prostration, Iblis's argument and respite, the tree, whispering, repentance of both, descent to earth.
quran:7:26 onwards addresses 'bani Adam' generally, so ending at 7:25 is a clean boundary.
quran:15:26-43 covers creation of man from clay, the jinn from fire, the prostration and Iblis's refusal and respite; matches the stated topic.
quran:15:44 (gates of Jahannam) continues the warning but is not about Adam; boundary acceptable. Note 15:43 mentions Jahannam, handle framing for young children.
quran:17:61-65 is the prostration and Iblis's refusal and threat against Adam's descendants; on topic.
quran:17:60 and 17:66 are unrelated to Adam, so boundaries are clean.
quran:18:50 is a single self-contained ayah stating Iblis was of the jinn and refused to prostrate to Adam; matches stated topic exactly.
Neighbours quran:18:49 and 18:51 are not about Adam.
quran:20:115-123 covers the covenant and forgetting, prostration, warning about Iblis, whispering, eating, repentance and descent.
quran:20:124 onward is a general warning to those who turn away; ending at 20:123 is reasonable.
quran:38:71-85 is the creation-from-clay announcement, prostration, Iblis's refusal, respite and oath; on topic.
quran:38:86 turns to the Prophet's address; clean end. Note 38:85 mentions filling Jahannam, frame carefully for children.
quran:2:124-132 are about Ibrahim: imamate, the House, the prayer for Makkah, raising the foundations with Ismail, the milla, and his wasiyya to his sons.
quran:2:133 centres on Yaqub at his death (Ibrahim named only as ancestor); acceptable as continuation of the wasiyya theme but worth knowing.
The milla theme continues in quran:2:135 and 2:140; not required for this range.
quran:2:259 is about a different man ('the one who passed by a town') who was made to die for a hundred years; he is not Ibrahim and Ibrahim is not named in that ayah.
Mapping 2:258-260 wholesale to prophet 'ibrahim' risks retrieval attributing the hundred-year sleep and the donkey to Ibrahim.
quran:2:258 (the debate) and quran:2:260 (the four birds) are correctly about Ibrahim.
suggested_fix: Split into two ranges for ibrahim: quran:2:258 and quran:2:260; exclude quran:2:259 from the ibrahim map (or map it separately without a prophet attribution).

reasons: quran:3:65-68 is the argument about Ibrahim with Ahl al-Kitab and the statement of his hanif milla; matches topic.
quran:3:64 is a general call and 3:69 moves on; boundaries fine.
quran:6:74-83 covers Ibrahim with Azar, the star, moon and sun reasoning, the argument with his people and 'this is Our argument given to Ibrahim'.
quran:6:84 (gift of Ishaq and Yaqub, then a list of prophets) is a related neighbour but moves to a list of other prophets; ending at 6:83 is defensible.
quran:11:69-76 is the guests, the calf, the good news of Ishaq and Yaqub, and Ibrahim pleading for Lut's people.
quran:11:77 begins the Lut episode; clean end. Ayat 11:74 and 11:76 mention Lut's people only as context.
quran:14:35-41 is Ibrahim's supplication for Makkah, his offspring, prayer and forgiveness; matches topic.
quran:14:34 and 14:42 are not part of the supplication.
quran:15:51-60 is the guests of Ibrahim, the news of a knowledgeable son and the messengers' mission to Lut's people.
quran:15:61 begins the Lut scene; clean end.
quran:19:41-50 is the complete dialogue with his father, his withdrawal, and the gift of Ishaq and Yaqub.
quran:19:51 starts Musa; clean boundaries. Note 19:46 contains the father's threat to stone him; frame gently.
quran:21:51-73 is the idols dialogue, breaking the idols, the fire made cool, rescue with Lut, and gift of Ishaq and Yaqub.
quran:21:74 begins Lut's own passage; clean end. Lut appears in 21:71 only as rescued with Ibrahim.
quran:26:69-89 is Ibrahim's dialogue with his father and people and his supplication; matches topic.
quran:26:90 onward describes the Day of Judgement (arguably continuing the passage to 26:104), but ending at 26:89 closes Ibrahim's speech cleanly.
quran:29:16-27 covers Ibrahim's call, rescue from the fire, Lut believing in him, emigration and the gift of Ishaq and Yaqub.
quran:29:18-23 are often read as a parenthetical address; they remain in context. quran:29:28 starts Lut; clean end.
quran:37:83-113 covers the idols, the fire, emigration, the son and the sacrifice ransom, and the good news of Ishaq.
quran:37:82 ends Nuh and 37:114 starts Musa and Harun; boundaries are exact.
Child-sensitivity note: 37:102-107 (the dream of sacrifice) needs careful, reassuring framing for ages 7-11.
quran:51:24-37 is the honoured guests, the calf, the good news of a son, and the guests' mission against Lut's people.
51:32-37 describe the fate of Lut's town rather than Ibrahim, but they are the guests' answer to Ibrahim; quran:51:38 turns to Musa.
quran:60:4 ends mid-supplication of Ibrahim and those with him; quran:60:5 continues the same du'a and 60:6 restates the 'good example', so an obviously relevant neighbour is cut off.

60:4 includes open disavowal and 'enmity and hatred forever' toward the people until they believe; for ages 7-11 this needs careful framing and should not be retrieved alone as a lesson on 'al-uswa al-hasana'.
suggested_fix: Extend the range to quran:60:4-6 and have a human reviewer confirm the child framing of the disavowal wording.

reasons: quran:28:3-13 covers Pharaoh's tyranny, the revelation to Musa's mother, casting him in the river, his adoption, his sister and return to his mother.
Clean boundaries (28:2 is the surah opening, 28:14 his maturity). Note 28:4 mentions slaughter of sons; frame gently.
quran:28:14-28 covers the fight and accidental killing, flight, arrival at Madyan, watering for the two women and the marriage contract; matches 'going to Madyan'.
Child-sensitivity note: 28:15 and 28:19 describe a man being struck dead; needs careful framing.
quran:28:29-35 is the fire at Tur, the call, staff and hand signs, Harun as helper and the promise of support.
quran:28:36 starts the confrontation with Pharaoh; clean end.
quran:20:9-36 is the fire, the call at Tuwa, the staff and hand signs, the command to go to Pharaoh and Musa's du'a for Harun; matches topic.
quran:20:37 begins the recounting of earlier favours; clean end.
quran:20:37-54 covers the earlier favour (the chest and river, return to his mother, Madyan), the sending of Musa and Harun and the first exchange with Pharaoh.
Minor boundary note: quran:20:55 still continues the description of Allah in 20:53-54 but is placed at the start of map-musa-06.
quran:20:56-76 is the appointment, contest with the magicians, their prostration and faith, and Pharaoh's threat; matches topic.
quran:20:55 at the start belongs to the preceding description (see map-musa-05) but is harmless.
Child-sensitivity note: 20:71 contains Pharaoh's threat of cutting limbs and crucifixion.
quran:20:77-98 covers the night journey and sea, drowning of Pharaoh's army, favours on Bani Israel, the calf and Samiri, Harun's defence and the destruction of the calf.
quran:20:99 is a closing address; clean end.
quran:26:10-68 is the call, dialogue with Pharaoh, the magicians, the exodus, splitting of the sea and drowning; complete episode.
quran:26:69 starts Ibrahim; clean end. Note 26:49 contains the limbs and crucifixion threat.
quran:7:103-137 covers the mission to Pharaoh, signs, magicians, the plagues, drowning and inheritance of the land; on topic.
quran:7:138 begins the post-crossing section (map-musa-10); boundaries consistent. Note 7:124 threat and 7:127 killing of sons.
Most of quran:7:138-162 is about Musa and Bani Israel (request for an idol, the appointed forty nights, the tablets, the calf, the seventy men, the twelve springs).
quran:7:157-158 are about the unlettered Prophet (Muhammad) and 7:158 is his own address to mankind; retrieval could attribute them to Musa.
Also 7:161-162 overlap map-musa-12 content (the town and 'hitta'); acceptable but duplicative.
suggested_fix: Either split into quran:7:138-156 and quran:7:159-162, or keep the range but mark quran:7:157-158 as not about Musa so answers do not attribute them to him.

reasons: quran:10:75-92 covers the mission, magicians, the few believers, the houses as qibla, Musa's du'a, the crossing, Pharaoh's late faith and preservation of his body.
quran:10:74 is about earlier messengers and 10:93 moves to Bani Israel generally; clean boundaries.
The ayat in quran:2:49-61 are relevant: rescue from Pharaoh, the sea, forty nights, the calf, the Book, the thunderbolt, manna and quails, the town, the twelve springs.

Child-sensitivity and framing concern: quran:2:54 contains the command 'فاقتلوا أنفسكم' and quran:2:61 contains group-level condemnation (humiliation, wrath, killing prophets). Retrieved to a 7-11 child without framing, this could read as collective blame of a people.
Range boundaries themselves are acceptable (2:62 is a general ayah).
suggested_fix: Keep the range but have a human reviewer set child-facing framing rules for quran:2:54 and quran:2:61 (or split them out so they are not retrieved for simple 'favours' questions).

reasons: quran:2:67-73 is the complete story of the cow, including the resolution of the killing in 2:72-73.
quran:2:74 is a commentary on hardened hearts; clean end. Note 2:72 involves a murder; frame gently.
The range quran:18:60-82 is exactly the story of Musa and the righteous servant; boundaries are correct (18:83 starts Dhul-Qarnayn).

Child-safety concern: quran:18:74 describes the killing of a boy (ghulam), and 18:80-81 give the reason. For ages 7-11 this is a hard passage (a child being killed) that needs an agreed framing before it is retrieved.
suggested_fix: Keep the range; have a human reviewer approve child-facing framing for quran:18:74-81 (e.g. lesson-level guidance) before this range is used for answers.

reasons: quran:27:7-14 is the fire, the call, staff and hand signs, the nine signs and the rejection by Pharaoh's people.
quran:27:15 starts Dawud and Sulayman; clean end.
quran:40:23-46 is Musa's mission and the full speech of the believer from Pharaoh's family, Haman's tower and the believer's rescue.
Yusuf is mentioned in quran:40:34 only as a reference inside the believer's speech, not as his story.
quran:40:47 onward (dispute in the fire) is a continuation about Pharaoh's people but not needed; note 40:46 describes the fire.
quran:44:17-33 is the noble messenger to Pharaoh's people, the night departure, the calm sea, the drowning and the choosing of Bani Israel.
Musa is not named in these ayat (he is 'رسول كريم'); the attribution is standard but answers should not claim the name appears.
quran:44:34 returns to the Makkan disbelievers; clean end.
quran:79:15-26 is the full short account: the call at Tuwa, sending to Pharaoh, the great sign, rejection and seizure.
quran:79:14 and 79:27 are unrelated; clean boundaries.
quran:7:59-64 is Nuh's call, the chiefs' rejection, his reply, and rescue in the ark with drowning of the deniers.
quran:7:65 begins Hud; clean end.
quran:10:71-73 is Nuh's statement of reliance on Allah, refusing any wage, and rescue in the ark.
quran:10:74 refers to later messengers generally; clean end.
quran:11:25-49 is the full episode: the call, objections, building the ark, the flood, the son, the landing and closing remark.
quran:11:35 is read by many mufassirun as a parenthetical about the Prophet Muhammad; it is short and inside the passage, so acceptable, but answers should not rely on it as Nuh's words.
Child-sensitivity note: 11:42-43 and 11:45-46 (the son drowning) need gentle framing. quran:11:50 starts Hud.
quran:21:76-77 is the answered call, rescue of Nuh and his family and drowning of the deniers.
quran:21:75 ends Lut and 21:78 starts Dawud and Sulayman; exact boundaries.
quran:23:23-30 is the call, accusation of madness, the du'a for help, building the ark, boarding and the du'a for a blessed landing.
quran:23:31 moves to a later generation; clean end.
quran:26:105-122 is the full Nuh episode in al-Shu'ara including the refrain ending.
quran:26:104 ends the Ibrahim section and 26:123 starts 'Ad; exact boundaries.
quran:29:14-15 states Nuh stayed among them a thousand years less fifty, the flood, and the rescue of those in the ship.
quran:29:16 starts Ibrahim; clean end.
quran:37:75-82 is Nuh's call, the rescue, his offspring remaining, peace upon Nuh and the drowning of the others.
quran:37:83 starts Ibrahim; exact boundary.
quran:54:9-17 covers the denial, Nuh's du'a, the flood from sky and earth, the vessel of planks and the lesson.
quran:54:17 is the surah's general refrain but closes the section; 54:18 starts 'Ad.
quran:71:1-28 is the whole surah, entirely about Nuh's call night and day, his reasoning, the idols named, the drowning and his final du'a.
Child-sensitivity note: 71:25-27 (drowning then fire, du'a against the disbelievers) needs careful framing.
quran:12:4-6 is Yusuf's dream, Yaqub's warning not to tell his brothers, and the promise of being chosen and taught interpretation.
quran:12:3 is the surah's introduction and 12:7 opens the brothers' plot; clean boundaries.
